card.title: Animal behavior: Reflex action, taxes, dominance and lead…

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Behaviour spans reflexes, oriented movements, social order and mass movement. Reflex actions — rapid, involuntary responses through the five-part reflex arc (receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron, effector) — bypass the brain, as in the knee-jerk. Taxes orient the whole animal toward or away from stimuli: moths to light, sperm to egg chemicals, earthworms to gravity and touch.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Reflex arc order: receptor → sensory neuron → coordinator → motor neuron → effector.
Sign of a taxis: positive = toward the stimulus, negative = away from it.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Taxis vs tropism:** taxis is the whole animal orienting its movement; tropism is a plant's growth response.  ·  **Anadromous vs catadromous:** anadromous fish spawn in rivers after living at sea (salmon); catadromous fish spawn at sea after living in rivers (eel).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Name the stimulus in the taxis: photo, chemo, geo or thigmo.  ·  Do not call a reflex a taxis. One is a body response through a nerve arc. The other is locomotion aimed at a stimulus.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Knee-jerk reflex*** — spinal reflex arc with only two synapse levels.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: No verified PYQ in the bank; practise reflex arc, taxes and migration as NEB-style practice.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Label a five-part reflex arc.  ·  Sort four behaviours into reflex, taxis and kinesis.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Receptor-sensory-cord-motor-effector — the reflex arc in five words."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** Distinguish anadromous from catadromous migration. **Answer.** **Anadromous** — fish that live most of their life at sea and migrate **up rivers to spawn** (salmon, Hilsa). **Catadromous** — fish that live in rivers and migrate **to the sea to spawn** (eel).…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Dominance ≠ leadership:** one is won by force, the other earned by knowledge — a group can have different individuals in each role.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Reflex arc: receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector; rapid, involuntary; brain bypassed.  ·  Taxes: photo-, chemo-, geo-, thigmo-, rheo-, thermotaxis — oriented movement toward (+) or away (−) from a stimulus.  ·  Dominance hierarchy: peck order, priority access, reduces fighting. Leadership: guides by experience/knowledge (elephant matriarch).  ·  Fish migration: anadromous (salmon, sea→river), catadromous (eel, river→sea). Bird migration: photoperiod-triggered; sun/star/magnetic navigation; demoiselle crane over Himalaya.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The bar-headed goose crosses the Himalaya at altitudes near 8,000 m — the highest bird migration known.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Why Animals Move and Act Behaviour is the coordinated response of an organism to stimuli. Some responses are hard-wired reflexes; others are oriented movements (taxes); some are social (dominance and leadership); and some move whole populations across continents (fish and bird migration). The syllabus groups them here.  ·  ## 2.
